text: The access slice answers the case and queue list behind two surfaces and adds no operation: the extended session answer of GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session, and the CASE_RECORD branch of the authorise contract published by RWB-P4-E1037-CON under DP-08. RWB-P2-E2033-CON is a build-against contract whose row and filter tokens the answer must satisfy, never a run-time caller, because Architecture v5 slide 13 draws P3 to P4 by REST and no P2 to P4 call.
why: The WP records the contract dependency RWB-P2-E2033-CON while the architecture matrix draws the case service as the REST caller and draws no call from rwb-integration, and the context pack lists no authorise path, so one stated reading keeps the story buildable on Day 1 against a fake.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 4 and 12; _work/msr/context/P4.md REST rows; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08 and DP-13
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access contract owner at the baseline review of RWB-P2-E2033-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
impact: If rwb-integration also consumes the answer at run time, one row is added to 12.2 and one clause to the flow; no acceptance criterion value and no test case ID changes.

text: The session answer carries the elements caseRecordRight, effectiveScope, teamCode, regionCode, matrixVersion, maskingVersion and fields (each with masked or clear and no value), and those names are fixed by version 1 of RWB-P2-E2033-CON at its baseline review; the authorise branch keeps the path and the request and answer shapes of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and this story restates none of them.
why: The sources name the session response type, the four scope values and the capability-area list, and fix no element name of the right, the scope, the versions or the markers, so the names must be proposed and then owned by a contract.
read: Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-012 and T3.2; RWB-E2-033 section 12; Template and Rules R7.2 s12
confirm: rwb-access contract owner (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) and the rwb-integration contract owner at the baseline review.
impact: If other names are fixed, 11 and 12.1 and the row mapper change; no rule, no criterion value and no test case ID changes.

text: MSG-GEN-006 takes the platform unavailable text at the platform message standard, and REQ-ACA-006 is read without its data-lake copy because the lake is removed under DP-17, so the requirement is carried by the one extract record and its order alone.
why: The platform unavailable message has no text in any source read and the requirement still names a removed lake, so one stated reading keeps the document testable without inventing a message or a component.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 12 and 14; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 13 (no data lake); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17
confirm: Platform message standard owner and the reporting lead at the wave 2 review.
impact: One message row and the requirement note change; no criterion and no test case changes.

text: The scope of a caller is the default_scope of the widest role it holds, read against LOV-SCOPE, and the reading roles of the legacy authority table that the matrix names without a scope keep the scope their own role row carries; the CASE_RECORD right is the R letter of the matrix version in force and no role is given a right in code.
why: The legacy authority table names RW-PRODHEAD, RW-AUDIT, RW-CONDUCT and others with Case record R but no scope, and the target forbids a scope value in code, so the scope must come from the role rows and one reading is needed for a caller with two roles.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 3, 8 BR1 and 10; Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 role.default_scope and T3.2 LOV-SCOPE; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-07
confirm: rwb-access data owner and the security administrator at the load review of RWB-P4-AD003-APP.
impact: If the narrower scope wins for two roles, one rule clause and one precondition row change; no value of a criterion changes.

text: Masking version MASK-SIT-01 is the version in force in the SIT environment, a field with no covering masking_rule row for the role is marked masked with the default marker XXXX-XX-XX, and the answer marks fields and never carries a value.
why: The FSD names the version and the default marker in its masking example and fixes no rule for a field that no row covers, and the target forbids a clear value unless a row admits it.
read: Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-05; RWB-E2-033 section 8 BR7 and section 13; Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 masking_rule
confirm: rwb-access masking owner (RWB-P4-AD004-APP) and the compliance officer at the load review.
impact: If no covering row means clear instead of masked, one rule, one criterion and one test case change; the story would then need a decision and not a build step.

text: caselist.export.maxrows stays 10,000 as the legacy story assumed under DL11 and the page-size bounds stay 1 to 200, both as parameter rows of the rwb-case catalog read through RWB-P3-E1042-CON with the version in force; LOV-SCOPE and LOV-CAPABILITY are read through RWB-P3-E1043-CON; the paths and the parameter row names of both contracts are fixed in those stories, not here.
why: The legacy story marks the export limit as assumed and reads the page bounds as a validation rule inside its own flow, while DP-06 and DP-07 move every changeable value and list to rwb-case and the sources name neither path.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 3, 5 X2, 5 X7, 8 BR6 and BR7, 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 and DP-07; Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.2
confirm: rwb-case parameter and reference-data owners (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON) at the contract baseline.
impact: A change of the limit or the bounds is a data change and no release; if the bound is owned elsewhere, one precondition and one row of 12.2 change.

text: The service connects with the rwb-access login of the service template, holding grants on the rwb_access schema only, and it holds no case row, no queue row and no access-log table: the queue codes, the timers and the case facts come from the caller and the extract record is a decision-log row written by RWB-P4-E1039-APP.
why: No source read names the per-service login, the context pack gives rwb-access 5 tables and none of them an access log or a queue, and DP-01 and DP-02 forbid reading another service's rows and sharing one login.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 41; _work/msr/context/P4.md tables and REST rows; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01 and DP-02
confirm: ACE team, DBA and the DevOps lead at the deployment review of the rwb-access service.
impact: If the service is given a log table of its own, one table row and one write path change; the answer, the rules and the criteria do not.

text: This story adds no table, column, index or migration: role, permission and masking_rule with their matrix_version, masking_version and valid_from columns exist from the wave 1 baseline, and DP-15 has an instance here as the per-service sequence convention only.
why: DP-15 is in the pattern list of the legacy key, while the legacy story wrote no access table and the context pack gives the service its five tables already, so no migration is derived for this slice.
read: _work/msr/context/P4.md tables; Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15
confirm: ACE team, DBA at the baseline review of the rwb_access schema.
impact: If an index is needed for the version lookups, one migration file is added to the rwb-access sequence; no query, rule or criterion changes.
